author: Keystone Today
title: Sewickley woman sentenced to prison for bank fraud involving guardianship agency funds
text:
← Back to the wire
Sewickley woman sentenced to prison for bank fraud involving guardianship agency funds
Judith A. Hetzell of Sewickley received a federal prison sentence for bank fraud involving funds from vulnerable individuals under a guardianship agency's care. She must also pay nearly $81,000 in restitution after admitting to drafting fraudulent checks while serving as business manager.
A Sewickley resident was sentenced on Oct. 13 to two months in federal prison and two years of supervised release after being convicted of bank fraud, according to United States Attorney Troy Rivetti. Senior United States District Judge Nora Barry Fischer also ordered Judith A. Hetzell, 64, to pay $80,966 in restitution to her former employer.
Court information showed that between November 2023 and February 2025, Hetzell served as the business manager for a non-profit guardianship agency in the Western District of Pennsylvania. During this time, she drafted fraudulent checks against individuals’ bank accounts managed by the agency as part of its fiduciary services. The checks were made out to cash and to Hetzell’s mother and deposited into two personal accounts controlled by Hetzell.
Before sentencing, Judge Fischer said that although Hetzell had previously lived a law-abiding life, "her criminal conduct was quite serious in that she stole funds from the accounts of vulnerable individuals who, for various physical and mental health reasons, required the services of a guardianship agency." Judge Fischer also said that Hetzell’s actions put the viability of her employer at risk.
The case was prosecuted by First Assistant United States Attorney Carolyn J. Bloch.
United States Attorney Rivetti said the investigation leading to Hetzell's prosecution was conducted by the United States Postal Inspection Service.
